note: Read in a copy of the Children's Act, 2005 (passed 23 June 2005) that Rodra publishes, since the Ministry of Justice's site lists bills by year without this Act's text and GambiaLII didn't answer. Majority: a child is a person under eighteen (section 2), and no child is capable of entering into any contract except as section 14 provides (contracts for necessaries aside, a child's contracts are void or voidable, and no action lies after majority on debts contracted before it); so contracts in one's own name begin at 18, held as the age of majority (a reading: the Act doesn't name an age of majority in so many words, and no other statute setting one was found). Work: not held. The Act sets the minimum age for light work at sixteen (section 43) and forbids hazardous work for any child (section 44), but the general minimum age of employment lies in the Labour Act, 2007 (in force 21 January 2008), which wasn't reached, and neither text read says anything of child performers. Service: not read; no Gambian law calling anyone to military service was reached.
